hints.title: Length Monotonic Ordering
hints.text: A predecessor word always has length exactly one less than its successor. Sorting words by string length ensures predecessors are processed before successors.

hints.title: Single Character Removal Predecessors
hints.text: For a word of length L, generate all L possible predecessor candidates by removing one character at a time: word[:i] + word[i+1:].

hints.title: Dynamic Programming on Predecessor Chain
hints.text: Store the longest chain ending at each word in a lookup table. For each word, dp[word] is 1 + max(dp[prev]) across all valid predecessors present in the dictionary.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Graph DFS across all pairs without length sorting causes repeated exponential exploration.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting by length and generating L deletions per word takes O(N * L^2) time with hash table lookups.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that predecessor transitions are length-increasing and generate single character deletions.
